signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine (market frame for Oschadbank and Raiffeisen Ukraine)
signals.signal: NBU H1-2026 card statistics: the Ukrainian ATM estate stands at 15.8 thousand ATMs, up only 0.2% since the start of 2026 - effectively flat. Active POS terminals rose 4.3% Jan-Jun to 582,500 and card-accepting points of sale rose 13.9% to 699,300. Cards issued reached 153.2m, of which 61.1m (40%) were active in June, down from 65.4m (44%) in January. Cashless is 96% of card transactions by count and 67% by value (95.3% / 65.3% in H1-2025); c.99% of in-store cashless transactions use contactless/NFC; 21.1m cards are tokenised (34.5% of active cards). Total card transactions were 4,903.7m worth UAH 3,861.2bn, of which 4,707.6m worth UAH 2,587.3bn were cashless - implying c.196m cash-withdrawal transactions worth c.UAH 1,274bn still ran through the ATM/cash channel in six months.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine - 'Bezhotivkovi rozrakhunky platizhnymy kartkamy dominuiut - rezultaty pershoho pivrichchia 2026 roku'
signals.implies: A flat 15,800-unit ATM estate next to a POS estate growing 4.3% in six months says Ukrainian banks are replacing and upgrading ATMs, not adding them - the classic profile for recycler retrofits, ATM-as-a-service and managed services rather than greenfield hardware. Yet c.UAH 1.27tn still came out of that channel in H1, so the machines are not going away; they need to get cheaper to run. The 13.9% jump in acceptance points against only 4.3% more physical terminals points to softPOS/tap-to-phone growth - a separate POS/acquiring angle.
signals.likelihood: High that ATM refresh and cash-automation tenders continue through 2027; low that the fleet count grows
signals.followup: Pull the NBU infographic 'Platizhna infrastruktura ta platizhni kartky, I pivrichchia 2026' (published 18/08/2026 18:15 alongside the release) for the per-bank ATM split, and compare against the 31/12/2025 figure to date the inflection precisely.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine (binding on every ATM and cash operator, incl. Oschadbank and Raiffeisen Ukraine)
signals.signal: The NBU is putting a UAH 2,000 banknote - an entirely new denomination - into circulation from 04 September 2026. On 26/08/2026 it opened consultation on amendments to the Instruction on organising bank cash operations, to add the new denomination to the list of banknotes banks must surrender to the NBU and to fix the packaging-material specifications for the 2,000-hryvnia note. Written comments close 04/09/2026. The NBU's own 'banknotes in circulation' page still lists only 1000/500/200/100/50/20, confirming 2,000 is not yet in issue.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine - 'Proponuiutsia zminy do poriadku orhanizatsii kasovoi roboty bankiv' (draft resolution, impact analysis and comparison table attached)
signals.implies: A brand-new denomination is a hard, dated forcing event for the entire cash chain. Every one of Ukraine's c.15,800 ATMs, every recycler and every branch cash-processing machine needs banknote-validator firmware and template updates, cassette and denomination-mix reconfiguration, and re-certification against the new note. That is squarely Printec's cash-automation, ATM software/firmware and managed-services business, and unlike most roadmap items it arrives with a fixed calendar date. Banks that have not budgeted for it will need a vendor who can execute at fleet scale in weeks.
signals.followup: Open the NBU draft resolution PDF and impact analysis for the exact handling and packaging specs, then ask Oschadbank and Raiffeisen Ukraine directly who is doing their validator/firmware update and recycler recalibration for the 2,000-hryvnia note.

signals.entity: Oschadbank and Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine (named as two of four authorised banks)
signals.signal: The NBU names JSC Oschadbank, JSC CB PrivatBank, JSC Raiffeisen Bank and JSC PUMB as the four 'authorised banks' obliged to exchange the withdrawn 1, 2, 5 and 10 hryvnia banknotes of the 2003-2007 series for three years from withdrawal - i.e. until 28 February 2029 inclusive - free of charge and without limit. Those denominations ceased to be legal tender on 02 March 2026; all other Ukrainian bank branches carry the obligation only for one year, to 26 February 2027.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine - 'Banknoty, shcho perebuvaiut v obihu' (banknotes in circulation)
signals.implies: Both target banks carry a statutory, multi-year, over-the-counter cash-exchange duty that ordinary banks shed in Feb-2027. That is manual teller work in a network they are otherwise shrinking, and it is exactly what teller-assist cash recyclers and automated coin/note handling are for. It also gives a concrete, regulator-mandated business case for cash automation that does not depend on branch-closure economics alone.
signals.followup: Quantify exchange volumes handled per branch since 02/03/2026 and check whether either bank has concentrated the duty in a subset of branches - that subset is the recycler target list.

signals.signal: Per NBU data cited by Interfax-Ukraine, Oschadbank had total assets of UAH 518.87bn at 01/07/2026, second among Ukraine's 59 banks, with the total loan portfolio up 6.7% in H1 to UAH 136.83bn. But H1-2026 net profit was UAH 3.38bn - 2.9 times lower year-on-year - dropping the bank from second to fourth in the profit ranking behind PrivatBank (UAH 24.56bn, -29.6%), Universal Bank (UAH 3.85bn, +36.3%) and Raiffeisen Bank (UAH 3.57bn, -24.7%). Sector-wide H1-2026 net profit fell 32.0% to UAH 54.07bn and 11 of 59 banks were loss-making.
signals.source_name: Interfax-Ukraine - 'Naiprybutkovishymy bankamy v I piv.-2026 staly Pryvat, Universal, Raif, Oshchad ta PUMB' and 'Oshchadbank zbilshyv vydachu mikrokredytiv u I pivrichchi na 37%'
signals.implies: Oschadbank is the second-largest balance sheet in Ukraine but its profit fell almost threefold in a year, and the whole sector is down 32%. A bank in that position does not sign large capex hardware programmes; it signs opex ones. Pitch ATM-as-a-service, managed cash-in-transit/cash-cycle optimisation and hosted compliance rather than a fleet purchase - and use the 04/09/2026 banknote deadline as the entry point, because that spend is non-discretionary.
signals.likelihood: High - profit pressure persists with a 50% temporary bank corporate tax rate in force
signals.followup: Get Oschadbank's own H1-2026 interim report and NBU-filed statements for its capex line and its disclosed ATM/branch counts, which the bank's blocked website normally carries.

signals.signal: On 25/08/2026 Oschadbank announced a partial restriction of access to its electronic services after its internal security systems triggered: the mobile app and services for legal entities were temporarily unavailable, and the bank said it expected full stabilisation by 17:00. Ukrainska Pravda reports the bank attributed it to its own internal cybersecurity systems activating. Separate minfin.com.ua entries record Oschadbank announcing major system updates on 11/06/2026 and warning of possible temporary service interruptions on 29/06/2026.
signals.source_name: Interfax-Ukraine - 'Oshchadbank chastkovo obmezhyv dostup do elektronnykh servisiv cherez spratsiuvannia system bezpeky'; corroborated by Ekonomichna Pravda
signals.implies: Three separate digital-channel disruption events at Ukraine's second-largest bank in eleven weeks. When the app and corporate channels drop, the ATM and self-service estate is the fallback of last resort - which makes its availability, monitoring and independent failover a board-level topic, not an IT one. That is the argument for Printec managed services with SLA-backed uptime, remote estate monitoring, and self-service channels that are not dependent on the same core availability path.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that further incidents recur given the tempo
signals.followup: Establish what changed on 11/06/2026 ('major system updates') - if that was a core or channel platform migration, the incident pattern is a migration-stabilisation problem and the sales entry is different.

signals.signal: Oschadbank issued UAH 3.3bn of micro-business loans in H1-2026, up 37% year-on-year, across 2,596 loans (+27%), taking its micro-business portfolio up almost 20% since the start of the year to over UAH 7.6bn. It processed 2,799 micro-business applications in the half. Under its co-operation with the Partial Credit Guarantee Fund in Agriculture it issued 313 microloans to agricultural producers under portfolio guarantees totalling UAH 459.8m.
signals.source_name: Interfax-Ukraine - 'Oshchadbank zbilshyv vydachu mikrokredytiv u I pivrichchi na 37%', citing the bank's own website
signals.implies: 2,799 applications converting to 2,596 loans in six months is a high-volume, low-ticket origination flow that will not scale on manual underwriting. That is a digital onboarding/eKYC and automated document-and-identity verification opportunity, plus AML/sanctions screening at origination volume. The portfolio-guarantee mechanic with the agricultural fund also implies structured reporting obligations - a compliance/reporting hook.
signals.followup: Find the original Oschadbank release on oschadbank.ua (currently blocked) for the channel split - how many of the 2,799 applications arrived digitally - and identify the incumbent onboarding vendor.

signals.signal: Oschadbank transferred UAH 4.8bn of dividends to Ukraine's state budget on its 2025 results (reported 15/07/2026), and on 05/08/2026 OTP Bank, Sense Bank and Oschadbank officially joined Ukraine's open banking ecosystem.
signals.implies: A state bank paying out UAH 4.8bn in dividends while its profit falls threefold has less headroom for discretionary IT capex - reinforcing the opex/managed-service route. Joining the open banking ecosystem as an ASPSP means building and running compliant account-information and payment-initiation APIs with strong customer authentication, which drags in HSM/security, authentication and API security work.
signals.likelihood: Medium - open banking participation confirmed only via aggregator so far
signals.followup: Confirm the 05/08/2026 open banking accession against the NBU's own open banking register and any NBU news release - this needs a primary source before it is used in a pitch.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine - open banking regime
signals.signal: Ukraine's open banking regime is live and operating under NBU board resolutions No. 81 and No. 82 of 25/07/2025 (authorisation of non-financial payment service providers, and use of qualified electronic trust services / open banking certificates). The NBU's public third-party provider register currently lists 6 authorised providers - 3 PISP (payment initiation) and 3 AISP (account information). Banks act as ASPSPs and must expose compliant APIs, with strong customer authentication, information-protection and cyber-protection requirements set by separate NBU regulations.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine - 'Vidkrytyi bankinh' (open banking) page and TPP register
signals.implies: Only six authorised TPPs means the regime is at the very start of its build-out, so ASPSP-side API, authentication and certificate infrastructure is still being procured rather than already sunk. Printec's HSM/security and authentication offer maps directly onto the qualified open-banking certificate and strong-customer-authentication requirements, and the API security/monitoring layer is adjacent to its transaction-monitoring business.
signals.likelihood: High - register will grow, forcing ASPSP-side capacity work
signals.followup: Enumerate the six registered PISP/AISP names from the NBU register and check which banks they have already integrated with - that tells you which ASPSPs are behind on their API build.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine - AI supervision track
signals.signal: The NBU has opened a staged process toward sectoral recommendations on ethical and responsible AI use by financial-services participants, publishing a Discussion Document and inviting written responses on: key principles of responsible AI use, risk-based governance and human oversight of AI, consumer protection (transparency, justification, review/appeal of decisions), and requirements for data/models, information security and operational resilience. It cites its own November 2025 survey: of 208 institutions that responded, 64% reported using AI/ML solutions and 23% reported active use. The NBU states Ukraine has no AI law yet and that it is taking account of EU Regulation 2024/1689 (the EU AI Act). Next steps announced are published conclusions and then a White Paper for the financial sector.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine - 'Vykorystannia shtuchnoho intelektu uchasnykamy rynku finansovykh posluh Ukrainy' (supervision page)
signals.implies: AI governance in Ukraine is moving from optional to supervised, with the EU AI Act as the reference model. That raises the bar on explainability, auditability and human-in-the-loop review in exactly the places Printec sells: AML/sanctions screening, transaction monitoring and fraud scoring, and eKYC decisioning. A vendor that can evidence model governance, decision logging and appeal workflow has a compliance-led wedge that a pure-AI point vendor does not - and 64% adoption against zero regulation means a large installed base is about to need retrofitting.
signals.likelihood: High - White Paper is an announced next step
signals.followup: Download the Discussion Document itself for its publication date and response deadline, and check whether Oschadbank or Raiffeisen Ukraine filed a public response - that reveals their AI roadmap.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine / Sense Bank (read-across to Oschadbank and Raiffeisen Ukraine)
signals.signal: The NBU has launched unscheduled inspections of state-owned Sense Bank to establish whether there was interference with the bank's automated system during transactions placing UAH 150m of bail for former energy minister Herman Halushchenko, whether management instructed staff to do so, and whether financial-monitoring law was complied with. The NBU stated that persons in the case themselves admit that tightened regulatory and financial-monitoring control mechanisms pushed them to seek workarounds, 'including interfering with the operation of and switching off the bank's automated systems', and stressed that the NBU has no access to banks' automated systems - monitoring, analysis, detection and suspension of suspicious transactions is the banks' own duty. Sense Bank subsequently suspended its financial-monitoring director at the NBU's demand, the government dismissed the supervisory board chair, and the management board chair was called before the NBU qualification commission on 26/08/2026.
signals.source_name: Interfax-Ukraine - 'NBU pereviryt mozhlyve vtruchannia v avtomatyzovanu systemu Sens Banku'; corroborated by Ekonomichna Pravda
signals.implies: This is the loudest AML enforcement event in Ukrainian banking this window, and its specific allegation is that an automated financial-monitoring system was interfered with or switched off. Every Ukrainian bank board - explicitly including the state-owned Oschadbank - will now be asked whether its own monitoring platform is tamper-evident, whether disabling it leaves an immutable audit trail, and whether privileged access is segregated. That is a direct, board-sponsored pull for Printec's AML/compliance and transaction-monitoring offer, sold on tamper-evidence and audit integrity rather than detection rates.
signals.likelihood: High - NBU inspections under way; sector-wide supervisory follow-through likely
signals.followup: Watch for the NBU's inspection conclusions and any resulting supervisory requirement on automated financial-monitoring system controls - that requirement, when published, is the sellable trigger across all 59 banks.

signals.entity: Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine (JSC Raiffeisen Bank, RBI Group)
signals.signal: RBI's H1-2026 segment data show Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine at 256 business outlets on 30/06/2026, down from 295 a year earlier (-13.2%), and from 266 at 31/12/2025 and 298 at 31/12/2024 - while customers rose 8.2% year-on-year to 3.124 million and employees fell 6.3% to 4,814. Ukraine segment assets were EUR 5,251m (+8.9% YoY), loans to customers EUR 1,856m (+29.3%), deposits EUR 4,219m (+7.2%), loan/deposit ratio 43.0%, NPE ratio 2.73%, profit after tax EUR 70.3m for H1-2026 (down from EUR 104.4m).
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International - Q2/H1 2026 results data file, sheet 'UA', published with the Semi-Annual Financial Report 2026
signals.implies: Customers up 8% while the branch network shrinks 13% in twelve months, and 42 outlets gone in eighteen months, is the textbook trigger for self-service migration - the transactions have to go somewhere. That is the case for cash recyclers and assisted-service kiosks inside the 256 remaining outlets, digital onboarding/eKYC to keep acquisition running without counters, and managed services to run a thinner estate at lower unit cost. Loans up 29% YoY means more origination volume flowing through fewer physical points.
signals.likelihood: High that branch reduction continues through 2027
signals.followup: RBI does not disclose ATMs by country - get Raiffeisen Ukraine's own ATM/self-service count from its Ukrainian-language locator or NBU-filed annual report, and test whether the 39 closed outlets were replaced by self-service points or simply removed.

signals.entity: Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine (JSC Raiffeisen Bank, RBI Group)
signals.signal: RBI attributes part of the Ukraine segment's H1-2026 net fee and commission income decline (down EUR 10.7m YoY to EUR 27.3m, -28.1%) to currency effects and 'lower earnings from clearing, settlement and payment services'. General administrative expenses fell EUR 3m 'resulting from lower software depreciation'; Ukraine segment depreciation fell 16.0% YoY to EUR 14.5m. Income taxes rose EUR 17.2m because of the temporary increase in the bank corporate tax rate to 50 per cent.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International - Semi-Annual Financial Report 2026, Ukraine segment commentary
signals.implies: Falling software depreciation means a prior capitalised platform cycle is running off rather than a new one starting - historically the point at which a bank re-tenders. Combined with weaker payment-services fee income and a 50% tax rate crushing post-tax capacity, this argues strongly for approaching Raiffeisen Ukraine on an opex/managed-service model (ATM-as-a-service, hosted transaction monitoring) rather than a capitalised platform sale.
signals.likelihood: Medium - inference from the disclosed expense mix, not a stated plan
signals.followup: Check RBI's intangibles/capex note and any Ukraine core-banking or card-platform project disclosure, and confirm whether a replacement investment cycle is scheduled for 2027.

signals.entity: Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine (JSC Raiffeisen Bank, RBI Group)
signals.signal: Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine states that nearly 7 out of 10 accounts for individual entrepreneurs (FOP) are opened online, with digital account openings reaching 67% of new customers by end-August 2026. Separately the bank offers corporate Open APIs (Account Balance API and ISO Statement API) over HTTPS with JWT and OAuth 2.0, across sandbox, UAT and production environments, and references the new ISO 20022 payment standard.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine - news item 'Nearly 7 out of 10 accounts of individual entrepreneurs are opened online at Raiffeisen Bank'; Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine Open API page
signals.implies: A 67% digital-origination rate for SME/FOP accounts is a live, scaled remote-onboarding channel - which makes the bank a buyer for the verification and compliance layer (document and liveness verification, sanctions/PEP screening at onboarding, downstream AML monitoring), not for a first-time digital front end. The existing OAuth2/JWT Open API stack means integration risk is low and the conversation can start at the compliance layer rather than the channel.
signals.likelihood: High - already in production and growing
signals.followup: Identify the eKYC/identity vendor behind the FOP onboarding flow (BankID NBU vs Diia.Signature vs a commercial provider) and whether screening is in-house or bought.

signals.entity: Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine (JSC Raiffeisen Bank, RBI Group)
signals.signal: On 21/08/2026 Raiffeisen Bank opened a relocated branch in Bohodukhiv, Kharkiv region, after its previous branch there was destroyed by Russian shelling; the bank frames the move as maintaining customer service and employee safety. RBI's group commentary notes Russia significantly intensified attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure during winter 2025/2026, which weakened Q1-2026 growth, and that no indications exist that the war will end before the end of 2026.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine - 'Raiffeisen Bank Opens a Relocated Branch in Bohodukhiv'; RBI Semi-Annual Financial Report 2026
signals.implies: Physical points of presence in Ukraine are consumable assets that must be re-established fast and cheaply, and the energy grid they run on is a declared target. That is the demand case for rapidly deployable, low-footprint self-service and assisted-service units with autonomous power and connectivity resilience - the 'Power Banking' problem stated commercially. It also favours managed services with rapid redeployment SLAs over owned estates.
signals.likelihood: High - relocations continue while the war does
signals.followup: Establish how many Raiffeisen Ukraine outlets have been destroyed or relocated to date and whether relocated sites carry ATMs; and separately confirm the current status, participant count and technical requirements of the NBU/banking-sector 'Power Banking' resilient-branch network - it was not reachable this run.

Angles worked: (1) NBU as regulator/primary - payment statistics, cash-operations consultation, banknote register, open banking regime, AI supervision track; (2) RBI Group investor disclosure - the H1-2026 report PDF and the Q2 results XLSM were downloaded and parsed locally, giving clean primary Ukraine-segment figures including business outlets, customers, employees and P&L; (3) the bank's own site for Raiffeisen Ukraine; (4) Ukrainian-language press (Interfax-Ukraine, Ekonomichna Pravda, Minfin, FinClub, PaySpace) for Oschadbank, whose own site is hard-blocked. GENUINE GAPS, not quiet ground: (a) EBRD guarantee - could not be verified at all this run; ebrd.com is a JavaScript SPA whose search and project-finder return no server-rendered results to any fetch route, api.ebrd.com does not resolve, and without WebSearch there was no way in. This focus item is UNRESEARCHED and must be re-run. UNRESEARCHED as a named programme. (c) Core migration - no direct evidence for either bank; the closest primary signals are RBI's 'lower software depreciation' in Ukraine and Oschadbank's 11/06/2026 'major system updates', both inferential. The 15.8k figure is the national NBU total, not a bank-level figure. Confidence is capped at Medium throughout per the rules, and two inference-heavy rows are marked Low.
